MOUZ Take No. 1 in HLTV World Rankings After IEM Beijing Title Share page Esports News Report MOUZ Take No. 1 in HLTV World Rankings After IEM Beijing Title Sergey Demidov Head of News Department Fact checked by: Sol Fayerman-Hansen Updated: Nov 10, 2026, 9:47 AM Published: Nov 10, 2026, 9:47 AM 4 min read Editorial Standards Why Trust Us? MOUZ moved to No. 1 in the HLTV world rankings after winning IEM Beijing, reaching 912 points and sitting two ahead of FURIA in the update dated Nov. 9. (Photo by Joe Brady/Getty Images) MOUZ moved to No. 1 in the HLTV world rankings after winning IEM Beijing, reaching 912 points and sitting two ahead of FURIA in the update dated Nov. 9. HLTV reported that the rise of three places also puts MOUZ on top of both major ranking systems. The team had already reached No. 1 in Valve's global VRS at the end of October. HLTV said it is the first time MOUZ have led both lists since June 2024, with Dorian "xertioN" Berman and Adam "torzsi" Torzsas the only players remaining from that earlier roster. A Tight Top Five FURIA dropped one place to 910 points. Vitality fell one place to 836, Spirit dropped one place to 777, and Aurora held fifth at 552. Natus Vincere climbed two places to eighth, and The MongolZ jumped five places to 10th after reaching the IEM Beijing final , according to HLTV's table. The Beijing trophy was MOUZ's second title of the season, following BLAST Bounty Season 2 in August, HLTV reported. The same update noted runner-up finishes at BLAST Open Porto and ESL Pro League 24, plus a bronze medal at PGL Masters Bucharest. HLTV Top Five By The Numbers 912 Points For No. 1 MOUZ MOUZ rose three places after winning IEM Beijing, their second title of the season. Statistics 2-Point Gap Over FURIA FURIA dropped one place to second on 910 points in the update dated Nov. 9. Statistics 836 Points For Third-Place Vitality Vitality fell one spot, with Spirit fourth on 777 and Aurora fifth on 552. Statistics 5 Places Up For The MongolZ Reaching the IEM Beijing final lifted The MongolZ to 10th in HLTV's table. Statistics $1 Million At BLAST Rivals MOUZ's last event before the Singapore Major runs Nov. 11-15 in Hong Kong with eight teams. Statistics Next Stops: Rivals, Then Singapore MOUZ's next event is BLAST Rivals 2026 Season 2, their final tournament before the PGL Major in Singapore, HLTV reported. Esports.ru said that event runs Nov. 11-15 in Hong Kong with eight VRS-invited teams and a $1 million prize pool. No U.S. sportsbook odds were independently confirmed for this update. Sergey Demidov is a veteran sports journalist with over 18 years of experience covering international sports. Since beginning his career in 2007, he has reported on the Olympic Games (Sochi 2014), FIFA World Cup (2014), UEFA Euro (2012), World Cup of Hockey (2016), and Stanley Cup Finals (since 2017).

Before joining RG, Sergey was an independent senior editor at NHL.com/ru (2016–present) and contributed to Gazeta.ru and TASS News Agency. Currently, he leads RG’s global news desk, overseeing correspondents across North America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and South America.

He has conducted one-on-one interviews with elite athletes, including Jaromir Jagr and Alex Ovechkin, former WADA and FIFA presidents Craig Reedie and Sepp Blatter, and soccer coaches like Fabio Capello.

Sergey’s editorial work emphasizes accuracy, sourcing transparency, and a neutral voice, aligned with the Trust Project and Google Publisher Center principles.

He is bilingual in English and Russian, specializing in NHL hockey.
